summary: William Woodville Rockhill worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Lycée Condorcet, the École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr, and under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux between 1873 and 1880.

William Wright studied at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. A scholar in linguistics and religious studies, he held posts at UCL, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum (1861–1870), and served as Cambridge's Adams Professor of Arabic (1870–1889).

Willibald Kirfel was an Indologist who completed his PhD under Hermann Jacobi and his habilitation at the University of Bonn. He worked at the Bonn library and served at Bonn as a librarian, Privatdozent, and ordentlicher Professor from 1922.

Sinologist Wilt L. Idema earned his degrees at Leiden under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, also studying at Hokkaido, Kyoto, and USC for China Studies. He was professor at Leiden (1976–1999) and later Professor of Chinese Literature at Harvard.

Winfred P. Lehmann was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1937 to 1941 and held a post at the University of Texas at Austin from circa 1949 to 1986.
Winfred Robert Martin worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan studied at Cornell and the University of Chicago (JD, PhD). She held posts at Washington and Lee, the University of Chicago, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University.
Winston Kyan is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung (attested 2006).

Wm. Theodore de Bary was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia, Harvard, and the U.S. Navy Japanese Language School, and served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia from 1953 to 2017.

Wolfgang Franke was a Sinologist and historian who studied at the universities of Hamburg and Berlin. He held posts at Sichuan University and Peking University, and later occupied the Sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1977).

Indologist and linguist Wolfgang Morgenroth studied at Jena under Richard Hauschild and habilitated at Greifswald. He held posts at Jena, Greifswald, and was Professor of Indology (Sanskrit) at the University of Berlin from 1972 to 1994.

Wolfgang Schamoni is a Japanologist who studied at Kunstakademie Düsseldorf, Waseda University, and the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at Munich and Marburg before serving as professor at the University of Heidelberg from 1985 to 2006.

Wolfgang Schultz was a scholar of philosophy, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna. He was administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient and was appointed Professor and Chair of Philosophy at Munich in 1934.

Wolfgang Voigt worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He founded the Verzeichnis der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland and served as its General Editor from around 1957 to 1982.

Wolfram Eberhard was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Berlin and the Seminar for Oriental Languages. He taught in China, curated at the Grassi Museum, was sinology professor at Ankara (1937–1948), and sociology professor at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woosung Huh is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He received his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University from around 1985 to 1995 and held a post at the University of Amsterdam beginning around 1999.

Wu Hung is an art historian and Sinologist who studied at CAFA and Harvard. He taught at Harvard, Oxford, NYU, and the University of Chicago, where he became Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor in 1994.
Wulstan Fletcher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
